title: Canonical square-zero tensor-power boundary formula
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes, $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $I=j.\ker$ with $I^2=0. For $n\ge0$ and a global section $s$ of $N=(j^*L)^{\otimes n}$, put $F=j^*(I\otimes L^{\otimes n})$. For each $d$, let $\eta_d:L^{\otimes d}\to j_*j^*(L^{\otimes d})$ be the canonical tensor-pullback adjunction unit and assume its categorical kernel sequence is short exact. There is $\xi\in H^1(Z,F)$ such that for every $e\ge0$ there are a tensor comparison $a:j^*(L^{\otimes n(e+1)})\simeq N^{\otimes(e+1)}$ and an additive map $b:H^1(Z,F\otimes N^{\otimes e})\to H^1(X,\ker\eta_{n(e+1)})$. The canonical section boundary [lem-sc-module-section-boundary-exact] of the section obtained by evaluating $s^{\otimes(e+1)}\circ a^{-1}$ on $1$ equals $(e+1)b(H^1(\rho_F^{-1};\,\mathrm{id}_F\otimes s^{\otimes e})(\xi))$. Cohomology is module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and the boundary is [def-sc-module-cohomology-boundary]. Scheme, closed immersion, ideal, ideal powers, invertibility and tensor pullback are as in [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-pc-module-pullback]; the unit is [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction].

source.place: Tag 09MS, equation coherent-equation-ses and its section-power boundary calculation; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Put N=j^*L. The closed-immersion ideal sequence tensored by the invertible L^d is exact, with kernel M_d=I tensor L^d and quotient j_*j^*(L^d), by the unit-quotient theorem. Pullback commutes with tensors, so identify the quotient with j_*(N^d). The ideal I and M_d are quasi-coherent, and I M_d=0 because I^2=0. The annihilated-module theorem identifies M_d with j_*G_d, where G_d=j^*M_d is quasi-coherent. The affine-morphism cohomology edge identifies H^1(X,M_d) with H^1(Z,G_d). The given section s of N^n has a connecting class xi in degree n. The given short-exact kernel sequences fix the canonical units and hence their canonical connecting maps; their short-exactness is redundant geometric data, supplied separately by the unit-quotient theorem.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Set O'=direct sum over m>=0 of L^{tensor m} and O=direct sum over m>=0 of j_*j^*L^{tensor m}, with multiplication by tensor product. These are sheaves of commutative O_X-algebras: locally a frame for the invertible L identifies O' with a polynomial algebra in one generator, so its multiplication is commutative; the quotient O is commutative too. The degreewise surjection from step 1 gives O' \to O with kernel K=direct sum over m>=0 of I tensor L^{tensor m}; products of two kernel terms land in I^2 tensor L^{tensor (a+b)}=0. Apply [lem-sc-boundary-derivation-square-zero] to O' \to O. By naturality of the long exact sequence for inclusion of a degree-m summand and projection onto it, projecting the boundary of the summed sequence to degree m is the boundary of the degree-m exact sequence. Thus the image of s in the degree-n summand has boundary xi. Induct on k>=1: for k=1 this is xi; if partial(s^k)=k s^{k-1}xi, the Leibniz rule gives partial(s^{k+1})=s partial(s^k)+s^k partial(s)=(k+1)s^k xi. Taking k=e+1 gives partial(s^{e+1})=(e+1)s^e xi, where s^e acts through O on K. Identify the ideal-tensor kernel with the categorical kernel of the canonical adjunction unit. The inverse cohomology comparison gives the additive map b from H^1(Z,F tensor N^e) to H^1(X,kernel eta_{n(e+1)}). Transport the canonical derivation identity to that kernel. The canonical boundary is the triangle boundary of [def-sc-module-cohomology-boundary], preceded by the degree-zero sections comparison of [lem-sc-module-section-boundary-exact]. No lifting is asserted.
